title: Introduce RAG snippet gallery, typed snippet components, and live-edit playground
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a modular snippet gallery and live-edit playground for RAG authoring. New examples and UI components for embedding typed code snippets across TS/Python/Go; improves authoring UX and telemetry hooks. Backwards-compatible docs changes.
description:
Motivation: make it significantly easier for engineers and technical writers to create, preview, and reuse small, typed RAG examples (prompt + retrieval + tool call) across the docs site and quickstarts. This PR introduces a lightweight snippet component library, a searchable snippet gallery, and an embedded live-edit playground so authors can iterate on examples without a full local stack.

What this changes (high level): adds a 'RAG Snippet' component set that renders runnable examples (TS/Python/Go) with typed bindings, introduces a gallery index page with tags and filters, and embeds a sandboxed live-edit iframe that runs against a lightweight in-browser emulator for previewing retrieval calls and mock tool responses. The gallery supports copy-to-clipboard, per-snippet telemetry, and version pinning for example outputs so we can lock tests/evals to stable examples.

Why this is different: existing quickstarts show monolithic examples; authors previously had to maintain separate sample repos or copy/paste examples. The gallery centralizes snippets as first-class authored assets with metadata (language, components used, cost/latency guidance) and makes them discoverable and testable on the docs site.

Checklist: - [x] Add reusable UI components (SnippetCard, SnippetPlayground, SnippetMeta) - [x] Implement snippet gallery index and detail pages - [x] Add in-browser sandboxed emulator (mock retriever + stubbed tool handler) for live-edit previews - [x] Provide typed snippet templates for TypeScript, Python (async), and Go examples - [x] Telemetry hooks: snippet_open, snippet_run, snippet_copy - [x] Tests: unit tests for components and integration tests for the playground harness - [x] Docs: author guide and CONTRIBUTING snippet guidelines - [x] Accessibility checks for keyboard and screen-reader flow

Backward compatibility and scope: all changes are additive to the docs site. The playground uses an opt-in flag on a per-page basis (data-enable-snippet-playground) so we can roll out incrementally and avoid regressions. The snippet registry is stored as markdown-adjacent frontmatter files under /content/snippets and does not change runtime APIs.

Follow-ups planned (separate PRs): - sync snippet pin metadata to eval harness for automated regression tests (ENG-1839) - add server-backed snippet execution for private model testing behind feature flags - add a lightweight snippet linter that validates example runtime signatures and docstring prompts

Related: ENG-1824, PM-77.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice direction — can you clarify how snippet version pinning will interact with the eval harness? I don't want flaky evals if snippets drift.
Author (Ava Martinez): We'll add a follow-up that syncs pin metadata (snippet:version) into the eval harness; for now the gallery exposes a 'pin' field in frontmatter and a lock icon in the UI.
Sasha Patel: Playground iframe communication needs a nonce to avoid any cross-site leaks; add nonce+postMessage origin checks.
Author: Added origin checks and a per-playground runtime nonce. See commit e1f02b4 for the changes in emulator.js and SnippetPlayground.tsx.
Ravi Kapoor: Are telemetry events PII-free? We should ensure snippet content isn't captured.
Author: Telemetry only includes snippet_id, language, action (open/run/copy) and runtime outcome (success/error). Full snippet text is never recorded; added tests to validate that.

notes_for_maintainers: The snippet registry is intentionally markdown-first; to add snippets: create a file under content/snippets with frontmatter fields: id, title, language, tags, pin. The emulator is intentionally lightweight (no network) and should be safe for public docs. For private model execution, plan a server-backed execution path behind auth.
